latest_release.name: v0.4.0
latest_release.body:
Self-hosting no longer needs Node.js or npm on the host: only Git and Docker. Docker Compose now creates the Convex admin key, deploys Ignidash's server functions, and runs data migrations in one-time setup containers before the app starts. Thanks to @Robert-litts for starting this in #71.

## Upgrading (self-hosted)

1. **Back up first.** Use the same command as in v0.3.0, with the admin key from `CONVEX_SELF_HOSTED_ADMIN_KEY` in your `.env.local`:

   ```bash
   npx convex export --url http://127.0.0.1:3210 --admin-key '<key>' --path backup.zip
   ```

2. Update and restart:

   ```bash
   git pull
   docker compose pull
   docker compose up -d
   ```

   Keep your `.env.local`, the `.env` link, and the Docker volumes. On first start, Ignidash creates a new admin key from your existing Convex data. Users, sessions, and plans are kept.

3. **Clean up `.env.local`.** Delete the `CONVEX_SELF_HOSTED_URL` and `CONVEX_SELF_HOSTED_ADMIN_KEY` lines; the old key still gives full access to your data. Then run `chmod 600 .env.local`, because older releases left the file readable by every user on the host. Running `sh scripts/selfhost.sh` does the `chmod` and warns about a leftover key.

After upgrading, Node.js is no longer needed. Future backups use the Docker-only commands in [SELF_HOSTING.md → Backup and Restore](https://github.com/schelskedevco/ignidash/blob/v0.4.0/SELF_HOSTING.md#backup-and-restore).

To check that the upgrade worked, run `docker compose ps -a`. `convex-admin-key` and `convex-init` should show `Exited (0)`, and `app` should show `Up`. If the app does not start, `docker compose logs convex-init` says why.

## Changes

**Self-hosting**
- **Docker-only setup and upgrades:** `sh scripts/selfhost.sh --init` sets up a new install, and `git pull && docker compose pull && docker compose up -d` upgrades one. A new `ghcr.io/schelskedevco/ignidash-convex-init` image is published alongside the app image with the same tags, so the server functions that get deployed always match the app version.
- **Safer by default:** the app container receives no secrets and no admin key. The admin key lives in its own Docker volume, readable only by the setup containers. `.env.local` is created readable only by you.
- **Pinned Convex versions:** the Convex backend and dashboard images are pinned to a tested build instead of `latest`. They change only when a release moves the pin.
- **Rewritten guide:** [SELF_HOSTING.md](https://github.com/schelskedevco/ignidash/blob/v0.4.0/SELF_HOSTING.md) now covers:
  - quick start and everyday use
  - access from other devices, behind an HTTPS reverse proxy (including private certificate authorities), and on different ports
  - Docker-only backup and restore
  - troubleshooting by symptom
- **Fixes:**
  - Server-side PostHog settings now reach the app.
  - `selfhost.sh --init` rejects host names that would corrupt `.env.local`.

**Testing**
- Every scenario in the self-hosting guide now runs in CI with real containers and a browser: quick start, LAN access, changed ports, HTTPS proxy, backup and restore, key recovery, and upgrading from the previous release.

**Other**
- Development and CI move to Node 24 (Node 22 or newer is required for development).
- The income ID migration keeps existing IDs instead of overwriting them.

detail.readme:
Ignidash

An open-source personal financial planning app with AI-powered features.
Monte Carlo simulations • Historical backtesting • US tax estimation • AI chat & insights

Website • Discord • Self-Hosting • Image Gallery

---

## What is Ignidash? Ignidash is a web-based retirement planning tool. It focuses on long-term financial projections as opposed to budgeting and day-to-day expense tracking. **What it does:** - **Monte Carlo & Historical Backtesting** Run hundreds of simulations to identify risks and calculate your probability of success. Test against actual historical market data to see how your plan would have performed. - **US Tax Estimation** Model how withdrawals, asset location, and income changes impact your estimated tax liability. - **AI Chat** Ask questions, clarify results, and learn about retirement planning concepts with an AI chatbot that knows your plan. - **AI Insights** Generate educational overviews explaining how taxes, RMDs, Roth conversions, withdrawal strategies, and more affect your results. - **Compare Plans** _(Coming Soon)_ Create multiple plans and view key outcomes side-by-side to see how different choices affect your future. [Try hosted version at ignidash.com](https://www.ignidash.com/) ## Roadmap Ignidash is in beta and actively under development. Planned features: **Q1 2026** - ~~Modeling debt and physical assets~~ - Configurable drawdown order - State & local taxes, IRMAA surcharges - Roth conversions & SEPP **Q2 2026** - Custom financial goals & milestones - Support for planning as a couple - Track NW with real-time data (by ticker?) See [Known Limitations](https://www.ignidash.com/help#:~:text=Known%20limitations) for details. ## Tech Stack - **Frontend:** Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS - **Backend:** Convex (DB & server functions) - **Auth:** Better-Auth with Google OAuth - **Payments:** Stripe - **AI:** Azure OpenAI ## Self-Hosting with Docker Run your own copy of Ignidash with Docker Compose. You need only Git and Docker on the host, not Node.js: ```bash git clone https://github.com/schelskedevco/ignidash.git cd ignidash sh scripts/selfhost.sh --init ``` Then open http://localhost:3000/signup and create your account. [SELF_HOSTING.md](./SELF_HOSTING.md) covers using Ignidash from other devices or your own domain, upgrades, backups, and troubleshooting. ## Local Development ### Prerequisites - [Node.js 22+](https://nodejs.org/) ### Setup ```bash git clone https://github.com/schelskedevco/ignidash.git cd ignidash npm install cp .env.cloud.example .env.local ``` Generate secrets and edit `.env.local` with them: ```bash openssl rand -base64 32 # For BETTER_AUTH_SECRET openssl rand -base64 32 # For CONVEX_API_SECRET ``` ### Optional Environment Variables | Variable | Description | | --------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | [Google Cloud Console](https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials) | | `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_ENDPOINT` | [Azure AI Foundry](https://ai.azure.com/) | | `RESEND_API_KEY` | [Resend](https://resend.com/) | | `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `STRIPE_PRICE_ID` | [Stripe Dashboard](https://dashboard.stripe.com/) | | `NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | [Stripe Dashboard](https://dashboard.stripe.com/) | | `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST` | [PostHog](https://posthog.com/) | ### Syncing Environment Variables Convex functions read their environment variables from the Convex deployment, not from `.env.local`. Set them in the Convex Dashboard or with `npx convex env set`. (Self-hosted Docker deployments sync them automatically; see [SELF_HOSTING.md](./SELF_HOSTING.md).) ### Running Locally ```bash # One-time: select a local Convex deployment (or `npx convex deployment select dev` for a cloud dev deployment) npx convex deployment select local # Terminal 1: Start Convex against the selected deployment npm run dev:convex # Terminal 2: Start Next.js dev server npm run dev ``` Open http://localhost:3000 in your browser. ### Available Scripts | Command | Description | | --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | `npm run dev` | Start Next.js dev server | | `npm run dev:convex` | Start Convex dev server | | `npm run build` | Production build | | `npm run lint` | Run ESLint | | `npm run lint:fix` | Run ESLint with auto-fix | | `npm run typecheck` | TypeScript type checking | | `npm run format` | Format with Prettier | | `npm run test` | Run Vitest tests | | `npm run test:e2e` | Run Playwright browser tests against the dev server | | `npm run test:selfhost` | Check self-hosting scripts and Docker Compose configuration | | `npm run test:selfhost:e2e` | Build the Docker images and test every self-hosting scenario | | `npm run docker:build` | Build both Docker images from your working tree as `:local` | ### Testing Self-Hosting Changes If you change anything that affects self-hosting (Docker files, `docker-compose.yml`, `scripts/`, Convex functions, or `SELF_HOSTING.md`), run the same checks as CI: ```bash npm run test:selfhost # script and Docker Compose configuration checks (needs Docker) npm run test:selfhost:e2e # builds both images and runs every scenario in SELF_HOSTING.md ``` The end-to-end run also needs `npx playwright install chromium` and free ports 443, 3000, 3001, 3210, 3211, 3310, 3311, and 6791. To try your changes as a self-hosted stack: ```bash npm run docker:build # builds both images from your working tree as :local IGNIDASH_TAG=local docker compose up -d ``` ### Code Style - ESLint and Prettier run automatically on commit via Husky - A secret scan ([gitleaks](https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks), rules in `.gitleaks.toml`) runs on commit and in CI. It uses a local `gitleaks` if installed (`brew install gitleaks`), otherwise Docker; without either, the commit hook only warns. Run `npm run test:secrets` after changing the rules. - Run `npm run format` to format all files - Run `npm run lint:fix` to auto-fix linting issues ## Contributing - **Bug reports & feature requests:** [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/schelskedevco/ignidash/issues) - **Questions & discussion:** [Discord](https://discord.gg/AVNg9JCNUr) - **Pull requests:** Fork the repo, make your changes, and submit a PR ## License [AGPL-3.0](https://github.com/schelskedevco/ignidash/blob/main/LICENSE) ## Star History [![Star History Chart](https://api.star-history.com/svg?repos=schelskedevco/ignidash&type=date&legend=bottom-right)](https://www.star-history.com/#schelskedevco/ignidash&type=date&legend=bottom-right)
